notes:
Night 3 closed out all four of Tomasz's open questions decisively, so I'm skipping tonight's slots — I don't think more data would change the answer, and the handbook is clear the warehouse is expensive and slots shouldn't be spent past the point of diminishing returns.

Report 1 is the clincher on #3: 406 of the 407 December correction events share the exact same timestamp to the microsecond (2025-12-31 22:59:59.999999), spanning 59 independent tenants and 59 warehouses. Fifty-nine separate companies' warehouse teams completing independent physical stocktakes at the identical instant is not physically plausible — this is the signature of a single batch/system event (a bulk correction job, migration, or data-seeding artifact), not a genuine annual stocktake process. I'm now confident enough to tell Tomasz this should not be presented to auditors as "we run annual B2B stocktakes" without engineering confirming what actually generated it. It's also worth noting the event touched 59 tenants broadly, not just the 8 B2B ones — the value just happened to concentrate in B2B because their goods (desks, fasteners, etc.) are higher unit-cost; most other tenants' share of the batch was economically trivial.

Report 2 closes #4's remaining loose end cleanly: the 10 zero-activity "...Warehouse" sites hold exactly zero stock on hand — they're empty/inactive shells, not a hidden blind spot. Nothing to flag there.

Report 3 is the best closing finding of the whole engagement: the routine adjustments-per-distinct-variant ratio sits in a remarkably tight 1.054-1.137 band across all 11 merchant verticals — B2B, apparel, electronics, food, beauty, everything. That means the "routine discrepancy" stream isn't a product or vertical problem at all; it's a near-universal flat background rate of roughly one single-unit miss per SKU per year, platform-wide. Apparel's raw totals look large purely because apparel merchants carry ~6,000 distinct SKUs versus ~90-275 for other verticals — not because apparel handling is worse. This meaningfully refines (doesn't contradict) the original memo's framing and gives a clean, audit-ready headline.

I have what I need to write Friday's follow-up memo to Tomasz; no further requests tonight.
